findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute (unrelated to the fix)
findings.body: `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` became `time.Minute * 1`. This is unrelated to the deadlock fix and looks like a leftover debugging change. Every cleanup job now runs 10x more often: snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, short URLs and query history. The annotation cleanup is the job that contends with inserts on MySQL, so more frequent runs raise the chance of hitting the deadlock this PR tries to avoid. The per-run timeout is 9 minutes, so a slow run can also overlap the next tick. Revert to 10 minutes.

findings.title: Debug logging at Error level, including the full ID list, on every batch
findings.body: Each batch logs `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ..., "ids", ids, ...)` plus a second Error line after the delete. The same pattern is at lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579. Successful, routine cleanup therefore emits Error-level logs on every batch, on every run, even when zero rows are found. These lines dump the entire slice of IDs, which can be thousands of entries for large `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` values such as the 32767 used in the new test. This pollutes error monitoring and alerting and bloats log volume. The `"err", err` field is always nil at that point. Remove these lines or downgrade them to Debug without the full ID list.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when inlining IDs for large SQLite batches
findings.body: In the inline-ID branch, `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` re-copies the whole accumulated string for every ID. With a batch of 32767 IDs the string reaches about 250KB, so this performs gigabytes of copying and allocation per batch, and the test with 40003 rows runs it repeatedly. Use a `strings.Builder` (or `strings.Join` over formatted values) to make this linear.

findings.title: Placeholder-based IN list breaks for large batch sizes on MySQL/Postgres
findings.body: The old code deleted via a subquery with no bind parameters, so any `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` worked. The new code binds one `?` per ID, and only SQLite with batch size >999 gets the inline path. MySQL and Postgres have a hard limit of 65535 bind parameters per statement. A configured batch size above that now makes every cleanup fail with a 'too many placeholders' error, which is a regression for such configurations. The inline-literal fallback should also apply to other dialects, or the IDs should be chunked into sub-batches below the limit.

findings.title: Test case name no longer matches what it tests
findings.body: The case 'running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations' relied on state left by the previous sub-test, so it really was a second run. The refactor now creates fresh data (9 annotations, 3 per type) and runs cleanup once. It only checks that nothing is deleted when the count is already at the limit, not idempotence of a repeated run. Rename it, or actually run the cleaner twice.
